research_insight_text_link.research_insight_description: EarnIn is researching systems and methods for allowing employees to access and use money earned but not yet paid by their employer, as described in the title 'System and method for automatic routing of wages.' The abstract details enabling workers to utilize unpaid wages for paying bills, purchasing goods and services, and accessing their earnings before the traditional pay cycle ends. This area of research and development focuses on wage access and financial flexibility for employees.

press_references.value: EarnIn Launches Jobs Platform, Extending Its Mission to Help Workers Get Back to Earning Faster

product_launches.description: EarnIn launched Earn Better, a jobs platform integrated into its app that offers access to over 5 million job openings plus free AI-powered tools like resume and cover letter builders, interview prep, and job tracking to help workers quickly return to earning and find better-paying roles.

press_references.value: EarnIn Expands Into Payroll to Redefine How America Gets Paid

product_launches.description: EarnIn launched EarnIn Payroll, an employee-centric payroll platform integrating earned wage access, Live Pay, and benefits integrations to give workers flexible, on-demand access to pay while streamlining payroll for employers and providers.

press_references.value: EarnIn Launches Live Pay, the First Technology to Stream Your Paycheck in Real Time

product_launches.description: EarnIn launched Live Pay, a new technology that allows workers to stream their paycheck in real time, available exclusively through the new EarnIn Card. This innovation enables users to access their earnings continuously as they work, marking a significant shift in payroll systems.

press_references.value: EarnIn Debuts Early Pay For Faster Paycheck Access

product_launches.description: A service that allows users to access their paychecks up to two days faster, regardless of their bank.

overview_description.description: EarnIn provides a mobile application offering earned wage access and financial wellness tools. It enables eligible users to transfer a portion of their earned income, typically up to $150 per day or $750 per pay period, into a linked bank account, without mandatory fees, credit checks, or interest; optional tips are accepted instead. The platform also includes features like real-time earnings access through Live Pay, direct-deposit accelerations up to two days early, Balance Shield for overdraft protection, credit score monitoring, and a savings tool called Tip Yourself. The application integrates directly with users’ bank accounts and employment verification, and operates independently of employer payroll systems by design.

legal_proceedings.description: Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser is suing EarnIn, alleging violations of Colorado lending laws and disputing the provider's claim that its earned wage access product is nonrecourse.

press_references.value: D.C. Court of Appeals Leaves in Place Dismissal of OAG Claims Against EarnIn

legal_proceedings.description: The District of Columbia Court of Appeals refused the DC Attorney General’s bid to revive enforcement claims against Activehours d/b/a EarnIn, leaving in place a May 2025 Superior Court ruling that dismissed most OAG claims and found the AG exceeded its authority over EarnIn’s earned wage access product.

A federal judge in Maryland ruled against EarnIn (Activehours), finding the company is subject to state and federal lending laws, and declined to dismiss a class action lawsuit brought by users of EarnIn's services.

press_references.value: DailyPay pushes back against NY AG

legal_proceedings.description: Activehours, doing business as EarnIn, is defending a lawsuit in Maryland alleging it operates as a lender under Maryland law for its direct-to-consumer earned wage access product; in August, U.S. District Judge Julie Rubin in Baltimore denied EarnIn's motion to dismiss, and plaintiffs face a May 4 deadline to seek class certification.

press_references.value: Fintech EarnIn sued by DC attorney general over 300% rates

legal_proceedings.description: EarnIn, a fintech company, is being sued by the DC attorney general over allegedly charging rates as high as 300%.
A federal court in Maryland recently characterized EarnIn’s practices as lending in a consumer case, bolstering efforts to classify certain direct-to-consumer EWA as loans.

about_short_description.short_description: EarnIn is an earnings management company that provides access to earned wages and financial wellness tools.

product.name: Cash Out
product.description: An earned wage access service that lets eligible users transfer a portion of wages they have already earned before payday, without interest or mandatory fees for standard transfers.

product.name: Live Pay with EarnIn Card
product.description: A pay-access and payment card offering that makes eligible wages available as they are earned and allows users to spend them through the EarnIn Card.

product.name: Early Pay
product.description: A direct-deposit service that enables eligible users to receive their paycheck in a bank account up to two days before the scheduled payday.

product.name: Balance Shield
product.description: A bank-balance monitoring service that provides low-balance alerts and can initiate customized automatic transfers to help users avoid overdrafts.

product.name: Savings Jars
product.description: A savings feature that helps users set aside money from their paychecks in a no-cost, FDIC-insured deposit account.

product.name: Credit Monitoring
product.description: An in-app credit monitoring tool that lets users view their Experian VantageScore 3.0 credit score and track credit-related progress.
